videos.title: Everything we knew about software has changed — Theo Browne, @t3dotgg ​
videos.description: For the closing keynote of AIEWF2026, Theo provokes you to think wider, not just bigger.  In this keynote from the AI Engineer World's Fair, developer and YouTuber Theo Browne (@t3dotgg) argues that the rapid evolution of AI models—moving from tool-calling (Sonnet 3.5) to long-running task execution (Opus 4.5) and now orchestration (Mythos)—requires software engineers to fundamentally change how they build products.  Key Themes: Rejecting Skeuomorphism: Browne compares the current state of software development to the design shift in iOS 7, urging developers to move away from legacy mental models and tools (like Git or terminal-centric workflows) that prioritize familiarity over actual utility (6:08 - 8:32). The New Tier System: Traditional categorizations of "side project," "startup," and "too big" have shifted. He highlights that tasks once requiring a dedicated startup can now be managed by simple automated systems, such as a Markdown file running on a cron job (10:33 - 12:20). Thinking Bigger: Rather than just building depth in a narrow feature set, Browne encourages builders to cover a wider spectrum of product functionality. Because AI agents can now handle significant parts of implementation, it is becoming viable for smaller teams to build products that compete with industry giants like AWS or Salesforce by architecting them for extensibility (13:12 - 15:30).  Takeaway: The barrier to entry for building complex, wide-reaching platforms has collapsed. Engineers should stop limiting themselves by legacy constraints and start building much more ambitious projects.  Timestamps 0:00 – Introduction and the "AI psychosis" experience 0:50 – Evolution of AI models: Sonnet 3.5, Opus 4.5, and Mythos 3:04 – The imperative to "go bigger" and push model capabilities 3:35 – Overcoming legacy constraints and developer habits 6:08 – Moving past our "skeuomorphic" phase in software development 9:30 – Personal project evolution: side projects, startups, and the "Markdown tier" 12:22 – Identifying the gap: What is "too big" anymore? 13:06 – Redefining the strategy: Building for a wider spectrum instead of just depth 14:50 – Scaling and architecting products to allow for user-driven extensibility

videos.title: Why Robots Suddenly Got Good at Everything (VLAM Explained)
videos.description:
Over the past year, humanoid robots have suddenly started folding 
laundry, sorting fruit, and handling eggs without crushing them — 
tasks that used to be impossible for machines. It wasn't a 
breakthrough in motors or metal. It was a complete rewrite of the 
software running inside them.

In this video, we break down Physical AI and Vision-Language-Action 
Models (VLAMs) — the technology replacing decades of rigid, 
rule-based robotics with a single neural network that takes in 
pixels and language, and outputs raw motor actions in real time.

We cover:
– Why traditional robots were fast, strong, and completely "blind"
– What a Vision-Language-Action Model actually is
– How robots learn through imitation learning and reinforcement 
  learning instead of manual programming
– Why "generalization" is the real holy grail of robotics
– The big debate: predictable rule-based code vs. unpredictable 
  neural network black boxes
– What this means as robots move from factories into our homes

If you're curious about the real engineering behind humanoid robots, 
embodied AI, and where physical intelligence is headed next, this 
one's for you.

Do the viral robot videos make you optimistic about robots helping 
with daily life, or does the black-box decision-making worry you? 
Let's discuss in the comments.

#PhysicalAI #HumanoidRobots #VLAM #RoboticsExplained #AIRobotics #EmbodiedAI #FutureOfRobotics #MachineLearning #TechExplained #AIvsRobotics

Keywords: physical AI explained, vision language action model, VLAM 
robotics, humanoid robot AI, how robots learn, imitation learning 
robotics, reinforcement learning robots, generalist robotics, 
embodied AI 2026, robot neural network, AI robots folding laundry,

videos.title: College Degrees Are Dying | Here's Why
videos.description: Did AI just put an end to the university degree? What happens when a piece of paper stops being worth the fortune everyone agreed to pay for it? For sixty years, the university degree was the closest thing to a guarantee the modern world had. You borrowed more than the price of a house, and it always paid you back. That promise is breaking, and it started breaking long before AI showed up. This is the story of the degree: how it became a fortune, why it was already failing, and why AI is the pin that finally pops a sixty-year bubble. videos.title: I’m taking AI seriously, so I’ve picked up some new Apple kit ahead of rising prices.
videos.description: I’m 60. I’m not a developer. I’m building my AI world. I talk about AI and share what I do with it.  Most AI channels are run by 25-year-old developers. This one isn’t. AI Foundations is for non-technical people who feel left behind by the AI wave: practical tools, no jargon, no hype.  I build real systems with AI to solve real problems and reduce my workload, so I can focus more creatively.  If I can do it, anybody can.  Let’s get into the current RAM crisis. The rapid pace of AI is consuming the world’s supplies of RAM, chips, and storage. Supplies are low, and prices are rising. This isn’t just a tech-industry problem — everyday people are now being forced to pay high prices for RAM-based tech. Companies like Apple have held prices steady for as long as possible, but the floodgates have now opened.  My name's Glen. See you in the next video
